transcript.text: Here's a lesson from Chanel that has
made them billions of dollars. Luxury
brands like Chanel are masters of
scarcity. They only give one or two
select pieces per skew to each store.
And they do that because they don't want
anyone who's buying a Chanel to feel
like anyone else is going to have one.
And so even if you go in cuz you saw
something in the magazine, you go there
and they're like, "Sorry, we're still
out of that." Or they'll say something
like, "You know what? I'm going to call
one of our stores in Colorado and get
that overnight air ship to us." How
likely is it that you're going to buy?
Very high. And so because these products
are so scarce, they also maintain value.
And so when people buy these purses,
they can resell the purses sometimes for
more than they bought at retail. And
when a customer can do that, that's when
you've mastered scarcity.
